job.title: Philanthropy Manager
job.description:
Harris Hill is thrilled to be partnering with One Community Foundation Kirklees in their search for a Philanthropy Manager to join the organisation at an exciting stage of growth.

Location: Kirklees, West Yorkshire (field-based with flexible hybrid working)
Salary: £37,000 FTE (pro rata for 22.5 hours per week)
Contract: 18-month fixed-term contract, with potential for extension
Hours: Part-time, 22.5 hours per week (3 days)
Closing date: Monday 16th November 2026, 9am
Interviews: Week commencing 23rd November 2026

One Community Foundation Kirklees is a respected and ambitious charitable foundation dedicated to strengthening local communities and improving lives across Kirklees.

Since its establishment in 2010, the Foundation has distributed over £8 million in funding to local charities, voluntary organisations and community groups, helping to tackle poverty, improve health and wellbeing and create opportunities for young people.

This is a particularly exciting time to join the Foundation. With ambitious plans to grow its endowment to £7–£8.5 million over the next five years, the organisation is looking for someone who can help unlock new philanthropic opportunities and build meaningful partnerships that will make a lasting difference to local communities.

This is a newly created role offering the opportunity to really make your mark.

Working closely with the CEO, you will have the freedom to develop relationships, shape the Foundation's approach to philanthropy and connect individuals, families and businesses with causes they are passionate about supporting.

What makes this opportunity exciting?
  • The chance to shape something new: Take ownership of a newly created philanthropy role, helping to develop the Foundation's approach to major giving, endowment fundraising and long-term donor engagement.
  • Build meaningful relationships: Work with individuals, families, businesses and professional advisers to create exciting opportunities for philanthropic giving and establish partnerships that deliver lasting impact.
  • Make a genuine difference: Play a central role in growing the Foundation's income and endowment, helping to secure sustainable funding for charities and community projects across Kirklees for years to come.

What will you bring?
  • A background in fundraising, philanthropy, business development or high-value relationship management, with a passion for building connections and inspiring people to give.
  • The confidence and enthusiasm to engage with a wide range of people, develop new networks and turn conversations into meaningful, long-term partnerships.
  • A proactive, creative and relationship-focused approach, with the ambition to help grow philanthropy and make a tangible difference to local communities.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys getting out and meeting people, developing relationships and bringing new ideas to life. You don't necessarily need to come from a traditional major donor fundraising background; the Foundation is keen to hear from individuals who can bring strong relationship-building skills, commercial awareness and a genuine enthusiasm for philanthropy.

You'll be joining a small, passionate and collaborative team, with the opportunity to work closely with the CEO, influence the direction of the role and develop your profile within the wider community foundation network.

The role offers part-time hours across three days per week, with some flexible hybrid working available following an initial induction period.
Please note that candidates must hold a full UK driving licence and have access to a car for business use. Mileage will be paid.

How to apply
To apply, please send your CV and a supporting statement or covering letter (maximum two A4 pages) addressing how you meet the person specification, how philanthropy supports local communities and what motivates major donors to work with community foundations.

Please send your application to hannah.laking@harrishill.co.uk by 9am on Monday 16th November 2026.

job.title: Senior Executive Coordinator
job.description:
Harris Hill is delighted to be supporting a wonderful charity in recruiting a Senior Executive Coordinator. This is an exciting opportunity to join an established, award-winning organisation working across the West Midlands to support migrants, refugees, and vulnerable people.

As the organisation continues to grow and develop its services, this is a pivotal role providing high-level support to its senior leadership team and Trustee Board, helping to strengthen executive effectiveness, governance and organisational accountability.

Offered on a permanent, full-time basis, the position is predominantly office-based in Birmingham, with the flexibility to work from home one day a week. There will also be occasional travel to other sites across the West Midlands.

The Senior Executive Coordinator will work particularly closely with the CEO and Executive Director of Services, taking responsibility for complex diary management, coordinating competing priorities and ensuring senior leaders are fully prepared for key meetings and commitments.

You will play a central role in supporting the effective operation of the Trustee Board, including preparing agendas and papers, attending meetings and producing accurate, high-quality minutes.

You will also coordinate executive-level reports and briefings, manage relationships with internal and external stakeholders, and support a significant new asset development project involving a range of professional advisers and external partners.

We are looking for an experienced executive support professional with a strong track record of supporting senior executives in a complex organisation.

You will bring excellent diary management, minute-taking and organisational skills, alongside the confidence and judgement to manage sensitive information and competing priorities.

Previous governance or Board-level support experience would be highly desirable, as would the ability to prepare clear, concise reports and briefings. Importantly, this is not simply an administrative position: you will be proactive, intellectually curious and comfortable constructively challenging senior colleagues, following up on commitments and identifying potential gaps.

job.title: Chief Officer
job.description:
﻿Could you help older people live more independent, connected and fulfilling lives?

Join Age Concern Epsom & Ewell as our next Chief Officer and help shape the future of a much-loved local charity, ensuring older people across the community can access the support, advice and connections they need to thrive.

Chief Officer – Age Concern Epsom & Ewell
Location: Epsom & Ewell, Surrey (office-based at The Old Town Hall, Epsom, with some home working possible)
Salary: £40,332 per annum (£46,633 full-time equivalent)
Contract: Permanent, part time (32 hours per week)

About Age Concern Epsom & Ewell
Founded in 1947, Age Concern Epsom & Ewell is an independent local charity helping older people navigate later life, maintain their independence and enjoy better wellbeing.

Our services include information and advice, medical transport, befriending, home visiting, IT support, DIY assistance and social activities, helping people access practical support and remain connected to their community.

Our work is delivered by nine part-time staff, supported by a dedicated volunteer network. In the past year, the quality of our services was recognised when our volunteer community was nominated for The King's Award for Voluntary Service.

From helping people access information and advice, to providing companionship and transport to medical appointments, our work makes a tangible difference to everyday lives.

As we approach our 80th anniversary in 2027, demand for support is growing alongside the challenges of an ageing population. We need to strengthen our financial sustainability, review our services and resources, and adapt to changes in local government and partnership arrangements.

This is an opportunity to build on our strong community roots and long-standing relationships, ensuring the charity remains responsive, resilient and well placed to support older people for years to come.

As our next Chief Officer, you will:
  • Translate the charity’s strategy into practical plans, lead an initial organisational review and work with trustees to agree priorities, strengthen governance and build organisational resilience.
  • Oversee the charity’s day-to-day operations, finances and services, using evidence on costs, impact and community need to improve quality, efficiency and resource decisions.
  • Work with the fundraising team, legacy co-ordinator and trustees to strengthen existing income streams, develop new funding opportunities and support long-term financial sustainability.
  • Support and develop staff and volunteers, while building partnerships and raising awareness to extend the charity’s reach and ensure older people, families, funders and partners understand the support available.

Who you are

You will be a practical, thoughtful and motivated leader who combines strategic perspective with a willingness to get involved in the day-to-day running of a small charity. You will bring a warm, approachable and collaborative leadership style, with a genuine commitment to helping people and an appreciation of the personal, community-rooted nature of the charity.

You will bring:
  • Experience of leading people, services or an organisation and translating priorities into achievable plans.
  • Demonstrable experience of financial management, including budgeting, monitoring expenditure and making effective use of resources.
  • Experience of fundraising, income generation or developing funding opportunities.
  • Experience of managing or supporting staff and/or volunteers, with the ability to build an engaged and collaborative team.
  • The ability to assess organisational needs, review established practices and lead improvements and change constructively.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to work effectively with trustees, colleagues, volunteers and external partners.
  • A genuine commitment to helping older people live independent, fulfilling and socially connected lives, alongside a responsible approach to the charity's long-term sustainability.
  • Knowledge of charity governance and the responsibilities involved in maintaining safe, well-managed services, including safeguarding and health and safety.

Experience in older people's services, advice, health, social care or community support would be desirable, as would experience of partnership working with local authorities, health services or other voluntary organisations.

Above all, you will be a self-starter who can identify what needs attention, ask the right questions and turn ideas into practical action. You will listen, build trust and bring people with you, balancing the confidence to lead with the judgement to involve others in shaping the charity's future.

Why Age Concern Epsom & Ewell?
  • Make a meaningful difference: Help older people access practical support, maintain their independence and feel less isolated within their local community.
  • Shape the next chapter: Play a central role in developing the charity's direction as it approaches its 80th anniversary, with genuine scope to influence its future.
  • Build on trusted community roots: Work alongside committed staff, dedicated volunteers and a supportive Board of Trustees, with established community relationships to develop further.
  • Create lasting sustainability: Help secure the resources, partnerships and organisational resilience needed to sustain valued services for the long term.

Application

You will play a pivotal role in identifying new opportunities, building relationships with senior stakeholders and securing partnerships that support the University's long-term ambitions.

This is a broad, externally focused role, combining strategic business development, income generation and philanthropic fundraising with opportunities to support research, innovation and knowledge exchange.

Key responsibilities include:

To achieve this, we must build on our momentum, strengthen our foundations and maintain a clear strategic direction. As Chief Executive, you will focus on five key areas:

  • Leading: inspiring and driving the organisation, including our staff, volunteers and members.
  • Building: supporting and growing a diverse movement of individuals and organisations.
  • Influencing: encouraging the wider engineering community to support our agenda.
  • Delivering: developing and implementing plans to deliver the goals set out in our 2020-2030 strategy.
  • Resourcing: ensuring we have the funds to maintain our operations while building the funding pipeline to underpin growth.

If you are inspired and excited by what EWB-UK does, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: Director
job.description:
Help shape the next chapter of one of Europe’s best-known charitable rewilding foundations.

Location: Knepp, West Sussex
Salary: £55,000–£60,000
Contract: Full-time, permanent

Nature can recover. At Knepp, we have spent 25 years demonstrating what that can look like.

Over the past four years, Knepp Wildland Foundation (KWF) has grown into a charity with national and international recognition for its work in promoting the understanding of rewilding. We have an ambitious strategy through to 2030, a great multidisciplinary team, strong partnerships and a remarkable opportunity to share Knepp’s practical experience with a much wider world.

As two of our major initiatives become independent organisations, we are looking for a Director to lead the Foundation into its next phase. This is a chief executive role about consolidation, focus and growth: working with the Board and team to establish what we uniquely exist to do, strengthening our organisation, and bringing the entrepreneurial drive to take our core projects forward.

As Director, you will:
  • Lead us through a significant period of organisational transition and development.
  • Work with trustees and staff to establish KWF’s future size, shape, priorities and ways of working.
  • Put excellent operational systems in place and create clarity.
  • Develop and empower a talented team, giving people the confidence and framework to lead their own areas of work.
  • Strengthen financial resilience, fundraising and strategic partnerships.
  • Drive the growth of our core programmes in species recovery, education, and knowledge-sharing, and promote the Foundation’s work to funders, partners, policymakers and landowners.
 
We are looking for someone who:
  • Has significant senior leadership experience and is comfortable combining strategy with hands-on management.
  • Is operationally strong, financially literate and experienced in working with a Board.
  • Is an excellent people leader who can empower an already capable team through change.
  • Has an entrepreneurial spirit, strong fundraising and partnership skills, and the judgement to know when to pursue an opportunity and when to say no.
  • Is an engaging communicator and a constructive collaborator, comfortable working alongside a prominent founder-led estate.
  • Is genuinely curious about rewilding and nature recovery and respects evidence and specialist expertise.

You do not need to be an ecologist or conservation specialist. We are looking first and foremost for an exceptional organisational leader who is excited by what Knepp has demonstrated and by the opportunity to translate that experience into wider change.

Why Knepp Wildland Foundation?
KWF offers an unusually open opportunity for a senior leader. We are a young, agile organisation, free of decades of accumulated bureaucracy, with strong goodwill, an exceptional network, an engaged Board, a talented team and the freedom to shape what comes next.

Our message is ultimately about hope: demonstrating that nature can recover, sharing what has been learned and inspiring people to act. If you are an ambitious, grounded and collaborative leader who would relish helping to shape the next chapter of a pioneering charity born out of one of Europe’s best-known rewilding projects, we would be delighted to hear from you.

Could you lead a charity with deep roots and a strong sense of community into its next chapter – creating greater opportunities for people with disabilities and/or neurodiversity to thrive?

Location: White Lodge, Chertsey, KT16 0FA (hybrid, minimum 3 days a week in the office)
Salary: circa £75,000
Contract: Permanent, full time, 37.5 hours per week

About us
White Lodge is a leading charity supporting children, young people and adults with disabilities and their families. With more than 60 years’ history, we support over 2,500 people across Surrey and beyond through specialist services and facilities in Chertsey.

White Lodge is a community as much as a service provider, built around our values of ENABLE: Equity, Nurture, Advocacy, Belonging, Language and Empathy. Our Active Plan 2025–30 sets four ambitions: Enhance accessibility and social opportunities; Champion customers' voices in health and social care; Transform local attitudes; and Strengthen its resources.

With strong systems, governance and a diversified income base, White Lodge is well placed for its next phase. The new CEO will provide continuity while bringing strategic, operational and entrepreneurial leadership to respond to a changing funding environment and pursue new opportunities, including a children's services tender.

As our next Chief Executive Officer, you will:
  • Strategy & Impact: Deliver White Lodge's strategy, translating ambitions into measurable outcomes and impact.
  • Leadership: Lead and develop a committed workforce, fostering an inclusive, accountable and values-led culture.
  • Governance & Finance: Partner with the Board to ensure strong governance, financial sustainability and effective risk management.
  • Operations: Ensure high-quality, person-centred services and effective organisational systems and performance.
  • Income & Partnerships: Diversify income and develop relationships with commissioners, funders, NHS partners and the wider community.
  • Influence & Advocacy: Champion customers' voices, strengthen White Lodge's profile and help transform attitudes towards disability.
  • Safeguarding & Compliance: Ensure high standards of safeguarding, regulatory compliance, equality and ethical leadership.

Who you are
  • A seasoned senior leader with significant experience in a complex organisation, ideally within charity, health, care or wider public services.
  • Experienced in leading substantial teams and complex services, with strong financial, operational and commercial understanding.
  • A strategic thinker with a track record of organisational change, sustainable growth and measurable outcomes.
  • Experienced in working effectively with a Board, commissioners, funders and strategic partners.
  • An emotionally intelligent, inclusive and entrepreneurial leader who builds trust, creates clarity and brings people with them.
  • A compelling communicator and ambassador, committed to equity, inclusion, dignity, safeguarding and ensuring lived experience shapes decisions.
  • Experience of disability, social care, children's services or another regulated service environment would be advantageous, as would commissioned services or significant tender experience. Previous CEO experience is desirable but not essential; exceptional Directors or Deputy CEOs ready to step up are encouraged to apply.

Why White Lodge?
  • Help create a world that is inclusive to all, regardless of ability.
  • Lead an established charity with a committed team, strong systems and strengthened governance.
  • Deliver the ambitions of the Active Plan 2025–30 and pursue new opportunities.
  • Work alongside customers, families, staff, volunteers and trustees who share White Lodge's values.
